ms.promise:
・Conduct research on comparable projects within other identity ecosystems and produce a write-up of the results. While we believe we have a decent architecture, we try to make the proposal as much aligned with existing standards as possible.
・Perform an architectural evaluation of the current design with consideration of the learning from other projects which may exists. In case we find an alternative architectural approach we’d like to keep the door open for a potential change request to achieve the same goal with a slightly revised architecture and components, if these means we can improve the overal impact of this concept, without reducing the promised feature set.
・Establish a GitHub repository with documentation on the project plan, including a README.md.
・License the project under Apache 2.0 to ensure open-source availability.
・Create a structured project stub, including basic API endpoints and frontend pages for the different modules.
・Develop foundational code blocks for handling W3C Credentials, including issuance and verification processes.
・Implement initial test suites and tests for core functionalities concerning credential handling and credential verification.
ms.criteria:
・A GitHub repository is established, containing a README and a comparison of similar projects in different identity ecosystems which may exist. Depending on the outcome of the research, there will also be an discussion on the different architecural options.
・The project is officially open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 license.
・Initial coding efforts for managing W3C Credentials and verification are underway and visible through GitHub commits.
・A dedicated test project within the repository includes multiple tests covering essential functionalities.

ms.promise:

・Implement code to manage different user roles (the owner of the credential (holder), who wants to publish a credential and the signer of an already prepared credential).
・Create a user interfaces for the credentials owners (holders) to register, create credential templates, and send these to potential signers, in case the credentials isn’t already signed.
・Establish an user interface for signers to accept prepared credentials from the future owners (holders) of a credential who want to embedd the credential on thier website.
・Design a basic verification API and webpage for credential verification, which is linked by the embedded credentials.
・Provide JavaScript snippets for credential display on websites and links to the verification page.
・Launch a demo website to test and demonstrate the general concept.
